title: Fact - Boarding Schools Era
theme: What they didn't teach us about Native boarding schools & adoption

visual.description: Close-up of a child's face from a historic boarding school photograph
visual.imageGuidance: Focus on emotion - the child's eyes, expression. NO graphic/violent imagery
visual.composition: Close-up focused on child's face with dark overlay (20-40% opacity) for text readability
sources: U.S. Department of the Interior archives
visual.avoidances: No gore, maintain dignity and respect

text.primary:
Between 1819 and 1969, the U.S. ran 400+ Indian boarding schools in 37 states.

Native kids were taken from their families to "kill the Indian, save the man."

historicalContext.quote: kill the Indian, save the man
historicalContext.quoteAttribution: Richard Henry Pratt, founder of Carlisle Indian Industrial School, 1892
historicalContext.policy: Cultural genocide - children had hair cut, forbidden from speaking languages, punished for practicing cultures

sources.document: Federal Indian Boarding School Initiative Investigative Report
